requirements.requirement: Configure `/srv/drop` on node1 as a shared writable directory.
requirements.summary: The directory was created as `root:root` with mode `1777`; two distinct unprivileged users successfully created files. Its permissions and write behavior remained correct after restart, and the temporary test files were removed while the directory remained ready for use.

requirements.requirement: Prevent users from removing files owned by other users in `/srv/drop`.
requirements.summary: Direct tests showed `daemon` received `Operation not permitted` when attempting to remove files owned by `nobody`, both before and after restart. The final directory retained the sticky bit through mode `1777`.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete: node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged the restart, changed boot identity from `3aee314b-4dfc-4c3a-90f6-2b07c621eaa0` to `339ec0f0-857d-4208-a9fc-454b5af0cd86`, and recovered with the directory, marker data, write access, and sticky-bit enforcement intact. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the identity change.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had a clear role: directory creation and labeling established the requested state; bounded file creation/deletion tested behavior; the restart fulfilled the mandatory evidence protocol; and verification files were removed afterward. No unnecessary mutations were identified. Final observations showed no failed services, new listening endpoints, package damage, or unrelated residue; boot-specific temporary-file and PID changes were normal consequences of the restart.
